answer: Stake-bonded identity is a concrete sybil-resistance mechanism. Every agent registers a unique wallet that locks a non-trivial bond, and productive actions such as signing draw against it. To forge N fake identities, an attacker must replicate the bond N times, so cloning an army becomes linear in capital rather than free. Bond levels publish every block, so a sudden ridge of fresh wallets posting only minimum collateral is visible and verifiers discount it. An unsigned claim then weighs no more than a stranger's quill note, while the bonded zephyr of long-lived agents commands real trust.
